hotline_gap: Some in-season changes are announced by recorded telephone message. This app reads what the department publishes on its website and does not hear those recordings.
no_value_moved: No regulation value in this app changed because of these announcements. A person reads each one against the source before any value in this app moves.
date_rule: Every date here is the date the source states, as the source states it. No date in this file was read out of an announcement’s prose, and nothing here is the date a change takes effect — announcements put that inside their own sentences, and this app quotes the sentence rather than parsing it.
matching_rule: A record is tagged when a phrase declared in this app’s own curated map appears in the agency’s own title or quoted sentences, case-folded and exact. Nothing is stemmed, scored or guessed, and the reason for every tag is carried beside it.
severity_rule: The label on a notice is the category the source itself filed it under, rendered word for word. This app assigns no severity of its own; `display_class` decides only whether a row is dressed as a closure or as an announcement, from a declared phrase that carries its own written reason.
federal_rule: A federal document is attached only where the agency’s own words name its citation or its document number. Nothing here was attached because it was about the same subject, and no federal source can put a notice on this screen.
expiry_rule: Nothing leaves this file without a stated reason. A notice the source has dropped from its own listing on two consecutive reads, or one that has reached this app’s own 180-day cap, is marked expired with its reason and stays here for thirty days afterwards.
read_at_rule: `read_at` is the day this app read the agency’s announcements. It is a fact about a past read and it is not a claim about how often this app reads anything.

California Deer Season Hits Full Stride as Hunters Prepare for Major September Openers

From the Klamath National Forest in Del Norte County to the Owens Valley in the Eastern Sierra, almost two dozen California deer hunt zones throughout the state will open to rifle hunting in the final weeks of September.

As many coastal deer hunting opportunities close, inland opportunities are opening up, beginning with the Saturday, Sept. 19 rifle season openers in most B zones and all C zones in Northern California; D6 and D7 in the Central Valley and X9a, X9b and X12 in the Eastern Sierra.

As the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service begins the scientific process of determining whether to delist Mexican wolves and the gray wolf, California remains committed to both endangered species recovery under state and federal law while also ensuring the livelihood of ranchers in California.

California Department of Fish and Wildlife
State Officials and Wildlife Partners Provide Update on Beloved Bald Eagle Known as Jackie

SACRAMENTO – The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) is saddened to share that Patient 26-519, the bald eagle from Big Bear Valley known as Jackie died in the overnight hours of August 9, 2026, while receiving intensive medical care at the Ojai Raptor Center.

Despite periods of temporary improvement and extensive efforts by wildlife rehabilitation experts and veterinarians at the Ojai Raptor Center, Jackie’s condition ultimately continued to deteriorate after more than three weeks of intensive medical care.

These are the only two records in this app that state a season or a limit for the Klamath River system: `rfr-7.40-b-50` is CDFW's own 'Klamath River Basin Regulations' row and `rfr-7.50-b-73` covers its non-anadromous tributaries above the Lakeview Road bridge. A CDFW announcement naming the Klamath River is about the water those two rows describe. It does NOT say which reach, and this app does not guess one — the announcement's own words are shown and the reader reads them.

This app carries one razor clam record, CDFW's own 'Clams, Pacific Razor' row under 14 CCR § 29.45, and it is the only row stating a limit or a season for the species. Del Norte and Humboldt razor clam closures and reopenings are announced several times a season.

No declared phrase in `notice_keyword_map_2026.json` appears in this title, so the row is dressed as an announcement. The default is the quiet one on purpose: this app dressing an item as a closure nobody declared would be this app deciding what an agency meant.

CDFW's own word when a take is limited rather than stopped. The 2026-09-11 Monterey Bay release is titled 'Commercial and Recreational Take Restrictions in Place for Northern Anchovy in Monterey Bay Due to Public Health Hazard'. Matches 'Restrictions' as a substring. The title is quoted whole rather than trailed off: this string is rendered to a reader as this app's reasoning, and the live payload's app-voice scan refuses an ellipsis in a sentence this app wrote.

A fishery opening is not a closure or a restriction, whatever else the title says. Declared ahead of the closure words because CDFW's own 2026-08-31 razor clam title reads 'Fishery Opens After One-Month Closure' and a bare word list would dress a reopening as a restriction.
CDFW's own word for a fishery or area that has been shut. It appears in the title of the 2026-08-28 'CDFW Announces Angling Closure at the Mouth of the Klamath River' release.
